Proof: According to the construction, $EBCF$ is a rectangular region.
In triangle $ABC$, the base and height are $BC$ and $BE$ respectively.
Hence, $\triangle$ region $ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times BC \times BE ... (i)$
In triangle $DBC$, the base and height are $BC$ and $CF$ respectively.
$\therefore \triangle$ region $DBC = \frac{1}{2} \times BC \times CF = \frac{1}{2} \times BC \times BE ... (ii) [\because EBCF$ rectangle$]$
Comparing (i) and (ii)
$\therefore \triangle$ region $ABC = \triangle$ region $DBC$ (proved)
Corollary 1. If the areas of triangular regions lying on the same base and same side are equal, the triangles lie between the same pair of parallel lines.
Corollary 2. Area of a triangle is exactly half of the area of a parallelogram lying on the same base and between the same pair of parallel lines.

Hints: In the figure, $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $AC$ as diagonal.
$\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle ADC$
$\therefore \triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times$ Area of parallelogram $ABCD$.
Theorem 37. Parallelograms lying on the same base and between the same pair of parallel lines are of equal area.

Let the parallelograms regions $ABCD$ and $ABEF$ stand on the same base $AB$ and lie between the pair of parallel lines $AB$ and $FC$. It is required to prove that, area of the parallelogram $ABCD = $ area of the parallelogram $ABEF$.
